content.body:
Captured with the fall of Czechoslovakia, the numerous and high-quality Czech tanks impressed the German High Command so much that they not only integrated them into the Panzer divisions, but increased production as well.
By June of 1941, more than 25% of the German armor was Czech-built. The high-velocity 37 mm gun, originally known as the Skoda A7, was better against armor than anything in that caliber the Germans had at the time. Even later, as the design reached the limits of its usefulness as a battle tank, the simple, rugged, and reliable chassis was the base vehicle for dozens of variants, including the fabled Hetzer tank destroyer.
The 38(t) is a superior light tank, with good mobility and a good 37 mm high-velocity gun. Due to its Christie chassis, firing on the move can be "boaty" and is difficult. The powerful optics and flat shot means that hits are generally easy and hard hitting. When firing from a halt, even full-applied brakes will allow the vehicle to shimmy slightly if still in gear, so a good tactic when halting is to quickly hit R twice. This kicks you into neutral (yet still will move forward if you shift up) without having to step down through the gears.
The 38(t) did have a weakness in its engine; turn it off whenever possible as hits with the engine running are far more likely to cause a catastrophic fire. Your commander is vital. Since he is also your gunner, it is rarely worth sticking him out of the turret for a better view. If he is unbuttoned, a single enemy with a pistol in the wrong place could effectively disable your entire tank as a fighting vehicle. Keep the commander down pretty much all the time. The one good feature about this is that in the 38(t) the unbuttoned commander does not stick out very far making him a slightly tougher target for snipers.
Control Variations: Crew 1 driver is on the right side of the tank, opposite to all other German vehicles. He has no periscope, while his main view is through a large frontal slit. He also has a view slit that is directly to his right, which you cannot zoom into but is nevertheless useful for formation driving. Crew 2 is a combination commander/gunner. When in the turret, he is a gunner (use numpad . or Del key to view through the gun sight, as usual). When unbuttoned, his binoculars are accessed with (numpad 0 key). Crew 3 is the loader, with no function. Crew 4 controls the bow-mounted MG in the front-left of the tank. He also has a view slit, numpad 0 or Ins key zooms his view while numpad . or Del key lets him look through the gun sight.
